open_points.subject: Project revision boundary
open_points.text: “A Project and a Customer carry a revision, an ordinal starting at 1 that every accepted change moves by one.” / “A project's last-changed instant ... does not move by: adding a room” / M01 lists “its rooms (M03), owned by the project” among the Project's facts.
open_points.question: Is adding a room an accepted change to the Project whose revision and last-changed instant must move, or is the room collection outside the Project's revision boundary despite being listed as a Project fact?
options: Adding a room moves the Project revision and last-changed instant.
Adding a room changes only M03 and does not move the Project revision or last-changed instant.
Rooms are not Project facts; M01 only projects or owns them without versioning the relationship.
open_points.default_guess: Treat rooms as separately versionless child entities: adding one does not move the Project revision or last-changed instant.

open_points.subject: Project–ArtifactPointer ownership
open_points.text: M01 says “The facts listed under a model are all its facts” and lists rooms but not artifact pointers; its lifecycle nevertheless says an anonymised project “keeps ... its artifact pointers (M05)”, while M05 says it is “owned by its Project record”.
open_points.question: Does a Project carry an owned collection of ArtifactPointers as one of its facts, or are ArtifactPointers independent records that only carry a project reference?
options: Add the owned pointer collection to the Project's facts.
ArtifactPointers are independent records linked to a Project; the Project carries no pointer-collection fact.
ArtifactPointers are embedded in the Project record but intentionally omitted from M01's fact list.
open_points.default_guess: Model ArtifactPointer as an independent durable entity carrying a project reference, with cascade removal when a Project is deleted whole and retention when it is anonymised.

open_points.subject: Audit subject for an import
open_points.text: M09 defines the subject “by identity only” and uses “the migration closure (M10) for the import”, but M10 classifies MigrationClosure as a value, says there is at most one, and gives it no identity.
open_points.question: What subject fact does an import AuditEntry actually carry when MigrationClosure has no identity?
options: A singleton migration-closure subject kind with no identifier.
The MigrationClosure's confirmation id as its identity.
The accepted file digest as the subject identity.
Give MigrationClosure a distinct Registry-minted identity.
open_points.default_guess: Use a singleton migration-closure subject kind with no identifier; keep the confirmation id and file digest as separate audit or closure facts.
